bug_semantics: Rendering a ScriptObject recursively stringifies each stored member value without object-identity cycle detection. A member that points back to its containing ScriptObject therefore repeatedly re-enters object rendering; because ObjectRecursionLimit defaulted to 0 (unlimited), the guard was disabled and recursion continued until an uncatchable StackOverflowException terminated the host process.
flaw_origin: cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e is the smallest real introducer. It changed ScriptObject enumeration to expose each stored value and added the ScriptObject-specific formatter that recursively calls ToString on that value. Its immediate parent lacks both vulnerable operations. The later a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d guard retained ObjectRecursionLimit=0 as the default and therefore preserved, rather than introduced, the already-existing vulnerable path.
evidence: Repository and advisory checks: `git remote get-url origin` returned https://github.com/scriban/scriban. The repository advisory https://github.com/scriban/scriban/security/advisories/GHSA-grr9-747v-xvcp gives the self-referential ScriptObject PoC, states that default ObjectRecursionLimit=0 is unlimited and causes a fatal StackOverflowException, lists 6.5.8 as affected, and lists 6.6.0 as patched; the assigned syndicated GHSA-PPRH-WGQR-2MMX/CVE-2026-74794 bundle describes versions before 6.6.0 as affected.

Smallest-BIC and direct-parent checks: `git show --format=fuller --patch cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptObject.cs` shows the same commit changing GetEnumerator from item.Value to item.Value.Value and adding `result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value));`. `git show 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634:src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` shows no ScriptObject-specific branch, and the BIC patch shows the parent did not expose the stored value. The advisory PoC's recursive edge is therefore absent in the direct parent.

Aggregate/import/move rejection: `git cat-file -p cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` shows exactly one parent, 790f00752e7b7392f2849452f37345852f313634, while the patch contains the functional additions themselves rather than an import or move. `git log --all --format='%H %P %s' -S'result.Append(ToString(span, keyPair.Value))' -- src/Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs src/Textamina.Scriban/Runtime/ScriptValueConverter.cs` finds cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e as the addition and 55a6d61fb656e87a49bbe49334236be558c5d3a1 only as the later removal during refactoring, so the later move is rejected as the BIC. No squash decomposition is needed.

Lifecycle and direct-fix checks: `git show a9affb64614358838aba16f28acb198f914e586d -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.Helpers.cs src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows a guard conditional on ObjectRecursionLimit != 0 together with the default assignment ObjectRecursionLimit=0 and documentation that zero means no limit. `git show --format=fuller --patch a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` directly changes that default from 0 to 20. `git cat-file -p` for the fix shows one parent, so despite its subject saying 'Merge commit from fork', it is not a merge aggregate and directly contains the closing change.

Version-boundary checks: `git rev-parse 6.5.8^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit}` resolved b640147b792c41aa3756b463673c741e46c44470 and b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7. `git diff 6.5.8^{commit} 6.6.0^{commit} -- src/Scriban/TemplateContext.cs` shows ObjectRecursionLimit changing from 0 to 20, and `git tag --contains a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4` starts at 6.6.0 and excludes 6.5.8.

Marker-state disagreement resolution: the primary encoded `ai_marker` as prose beginning `absent:`, whereas the reviewer encoded it as null. Re-running `git cat-file -t cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` returned `commit`, and `git cat-file -p cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e` showed one parent, author and committer Alexandre Mutel <alexandre_mutel@live.com>, and only the ordinary subject `Fix pretty print object ScriptObject and ScriptArray, dump objects with {...} and [...]`. The BIC commit object has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI signal. Therefore the canonical marker state is null: the reviewer's state wins, while the primary's underlying observation was correct but placed in the wrong field representation. No PR, branch, later commit, or fix-commit attribution was used.
reasoning: The vulnerability-first reconstruction isolates the recursive descent into actual ScriptObject member values, not the later optional guard, as the causal flaw. cae439abd6a3d1117cebdf128a028bbdb5126e9e writes that edge directly, has one parent, and its direct parent lacks it; the later removal found by -S is a refactor and not an origin. The direct fix makes the existing guard active by default, and both the first-party advisory and tag/tree checks establish the 6.5.8-to-6.6.0 vulnerable/fixed boundary. The only assigned disagreement is marker_state. The raw BIC commit object contains no AI attribution signal, so `ai_marker` must be null rather than a prose `absent:` string. This resolves the disagreement in favor of the reviewer's canonical state, though both audits agreed on the substantive absence and NOT_AI conclusion. With a verified BIC, immediate-parent absence, direct fix, release boundary, and BIC-only marker check, NOT_AI is gate-complete.
